events.text: The mind flayers of Ch'Chitl plot to enslave Waterdeep, but their efforts are ruined when githyanki make a surprise attack and mortally wound the elder brain.

events.text: The fifth Emperor Chin of Shou Lung dies following a hunting accident. In death, he is granted the deific name "Yeh Tu", meaning "Hare", leading to rumor that he was assassinated by a jealous family member. His grandson becomes the sixth emperor.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 126

events.text: The individual graves in Waterdeep are replaced by tombs, creating the City of the Dead.
cites: City of Splendors (boxed set): Campaign Guide, с. 30

events.text: The Gundwynd, Stormweather, and Wavesilver families are ennobled in Waterdeep.
Vine-blight ravishes grape orchards, meaning there is very little wine made this year.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition (revised), с. 17

events.text: The Company of the Black Snake is wiped out by a rival adventuring group, with Bedwyn Fayr and Pep Greenfields as the only survivors.

Summer: Poor grape harvests in the Purple Hills region of Tethyr precipitate the Wine Blight Insurrection in which peasant farmers refuse to tithe the usual quantity of wine to the Duke of Ankramir. Rather than surrender the wine to the duke's soldiers, the farmers broke most of the casks and threw them into the Sea of Swords. This came to be known as the Battle of the Broken Vats.
cites: Powers & Pantheons, с. 142

events.text: Due to growing undead problems in the City of the Dead in Waterdeep, this portion of the city is walled and a lasting curfew is enforced.
cites: City of Splendors (boxed set): Campaign Guide, с. 30

events.text: Mirabar is attacked by orc hordes but they are repelled by the militia, including Torgar Hammerstriker.
cites: The Thousand Orcs: MMP, с. 57

events.text: A plague ravishes lands around the northern shore of the Inner Sea, from the Great Dale to Cormyr.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 126

events.text: Daurgothoth, a dracolich known as the Creeping Doom, makes his lair in the abandoned subterranean city of Dolblunde.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 126

events.text: The ex-Lord of Turmish, Corwin Freas, is assassinated. The Cult of the Dragon are thought to be behind it.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 126

events.text: There are many assassinations this year, due to the growing might of thieves' guilds.
cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition (revised), с. 17

cites: Draconomicon (1990), с. 2–3

events.text: Priests of Bhaal travelling from eastern Amn slaughter all whom they encounter until they reach Westgate, most notably Raevarl's Circle, a group of Silvanite priests living in a small forest (that no longer exists) south west of the city. The Bhaalites are defeated by a hastily assembled mercenary army.
cites: Prayers from the Faithful, с. 51

cites: City of Splendors (boxed set): Campaign Guide, с. 30
The Grand History of the Realms, с. 126

cites: Undermountain: Stardock, с. 14

events.text: Daeros Dragonspear, the famed half-dwarf adventurer, explores the lost underground city of Kanaglym, which lies in the depths of the Duchy of Hunnabar of Phalorm. He seizes a hoard of gems from a beholder dwelling there and survives, then decides to retire. Daeros then constructs Dragonspear Castle at the site of the lair of the copper dragon Halatathlaer. Dwarves are welcomed there, and they settled in the castle's outer ward.

events.text: An orc horde destroys Evershed, a settlement south of the Evermoors.
cites: Prayers from the Faithful, с. 64

events.text: Khelben "Blackstaff" Arunsun, then known as "Khelben the Elder," leaves Waterdeep, but Blackstaff Tower is still occupied by his apprentices.
cites: City of Splendors (boxed set): Campaign Guide, с. 30

events.text: A tidal wave strikes Calimshan.

cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 128

During the last day of celebration, Coyo is ensorcelled and forced to volunteer for sacrifice to god Zaltec. The Revered Counsellor Zomoc's plan to remove a potential political foe is successful.

cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 128

events.text: Halacar, ruler of Aglarond, invades Thay. He marches his army along the River Lapendrar, but the Red Wizards of Thay obliterate his forces in the Battle of Lapendrar.
cites: The Grand History of the Realms, с. 128

events.text: Lapaliiya, meanwhile, tries to invade Halruaa via the Talath Pass, but the Lapaliiyan forces are repelled.

Their travels are dubbed the "Slaughter of the Crazed" but they are stopped by militiamen near Shamph. Many of the Talassans escape, including the one with the Chain, but their depredations, at least, are halted.

cites: Lands of Intrigue: Erlkazar and Folk of Intrigue, с. 29

The Guildwars end with the deaths of all but two in the Council of Guildmasters, Ehlemm Zoar and Lhorar Gildeggh, who agree to power-share, proclaiming themselves the Lord Magisters. However, their ongoing conflict limits their governance of the city.

cites: Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 2nd edition (revised), с. 17

cites: Ruins of Zhentil Keep: Campaign Book, с. 15,28

events.text: After several bloody battles between Ilmateri warriors working for the House of Holy Suffering and those working for the House of the Broken God, Lord Sir Jargus Holenhond of the Order of the Golden Cup demands the Tome of Torment be sent to Keltar and the leader of the House of the Broken God, Bloirt Waelarn, as the instigator of hostilities, be sent to live in a hermitage for the rest of his days. Holenhod's instructions are heeded and hostilities between the two temples cease. However, Waelarn kills the crew of the ship transporting him but not before a message gets out to an archmage, who forces the disgraced priest to his hermitage, horribly mutating him to prevent rescue and impede his casting of spells.

events.text: King Dhanar of the Parhek dynasty of Amn is assassinated in Athkatla.
cites: Volo's Guide to Baldur's Gate II, с. 13

events.text: The enchanted blade Albruin is stolen from Castle Obarskyr by the halfling thief Nypan, who manages to pass or sell it off before being captured and killed by Cormyrian soldiers in Wheloon. Rumors of the blade's whereabouts circle around a fence by the name of Blusken Shult, who may have transported it to a buyer located along some shore of the Wyvernwater, but this is never reliably confirmed. Albruin remains unaccounted for, for another 24 years.

The villagers, monks, and a number of monsters are forced to flee with all of their possessions through a portal opened by a powerful mage that takes them to Hesuel Ilshar on Oerth. events.text: A Calishite wizard called Ithtaerus Casalia plots to steal the riches of Dragonspear Castle, which is held by Daeros Dragonspear and his dragon companion Halatathlaer. Ithtaerus forces the dragon into a magical sleep, then tricks Daeros into sacrificing his own life and opening a portal to the hell of Avernus. Devils invade the castle, and are fought by Daeros's followers. Meanwhile, Ithtaerus loots Halatathlaer's hoard, but then goes on to lure three ambitious young dragons with news that Halatathlaer and his wealth are vulnerable. The dragons kill Halatathlaer and then each other, in the process obliterating much of the castle. The survivor, the black dragon Sharndrel, kills Ithtaerus in revenge before leaving.

events.text: In Sembia, a young, dissolute noble named Sterth Zelgarik, desperate to refill his coffers and avoid having to work for a living (after unexpectedly inheriting his family's estate and then squandering all his money on lavish parties and expensive courtesans), is tricked by a wily priest of Gargauth into a shady business deal that eventually culminates in him losing his soul to the demigod of betrayal and corruption. Transformed into a blackguard now called Krysus Vaant, he terrorizes political enemies and commits countless offenses and blasphemies against the church of Tyr until the most powerful Tyrran priest in Saerloon petitions his god to send a champion. The planetar Resounding Justice appears and, after a confrontation and chase outside Archenbridge, eventually destroys both Vaant and the pit fiend Tenflames by sacrificing her own life.

It is during this time that the goddess Chauntea notices the crippled and faltering status of the Earthmother and begins to counter Bhaal's schemes for the Isles.
